newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares continue trend, close higher.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares continue trend, close higher.

text.p: Delhi stocks consolidated the last three days' gains to close higher on Friday on strong buying by foreign and domestic investors, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's benchmark index closed 6.55 points higher at 911.98.

Traders said short covering by traders in tobacco and hotels company ITC Ltd and purchases by India's largest mutual fund, the Unit Trust of India, on the last day of the fortnightly settlement boosted market sentiment.

"A surge in most weighted stocks, Hindustan Lever Ltd and ITC, both multinational counters, stole the show despite Friday being the last day of current settlement," said Yogesh Sethi of stock brokerage Vinayaka Investments.
"Apart from blue chips, retail investors showed interest in B-group stocks with strong fundamentals," another broker said.
ITC surged 32.80 rupees to 539.85, fuelled by encouraging working results in the first quarter of 1997/98 (April-March).
The Business Standard newspaper said on Thursday that ITC had reported a 34 percent increase in its net profit for the first quarter ending June 30, 1997.
Hindustan Lever ended the day 59.90 rupees higher at 1,469.
Reliance Industries closed 2.85 rupees higher at 360.40 on speculation that the company might announce encouraging first quarter results for 1997/98, brokers said.
Mahanagar Telephone Nigam Ltd rose 3.95 rupees to 295.95.
Castrol India surged 54 rupees to 704 on speculation that it might issue bonus shares.
Carrier Aircon gained 22 rupees, closing at 292, on foreign investors' interest, brokers said.
